title: 13th Sitting of third session of 2025
summary: The sitting opened at 09:01 with 38 members present. Written ministerial answers were tabled, a first reading of a government bill to amend the Evidence Act was announced, and the chair said an urgent matter from the South Galolhu member did not meet the Rules. Members then debated a resolution from the Kendhoo member on delays in handing over the 4,000 Gedhoruveriya flats and related land plots, with government-side members defending the current reclamation plan and opposition members saying promises have not been kept. After a short break, Parliament voted 63 to 0 to approve Dr. Aishath Rameela as a member of the Human Rights Commission; the sitting ended at 11:08. The text layer is somewhat garbled in places and the numbering of items 6 and 7 is inferred.

items.title: Praises and prayers; opening of the sitting
Attendance of members
items.outcome: 38 present, 2 on leave, 6 on official travel

items.title: Change of committee membership under Rule 151: Milandhoo member Hassan Mufeed replaces Manadhoo member Husnee Mubarik on the Judiciary Committee
Written question from the North Galolhu member to the Minister of Construction, Housing and Infrastructure on the timeline for the Ha. Alif Baarashu harbour works
items.outcome: written answer tabled; concept plan being finalised, agreement to be signed in November 2025, works expected to take about 2 years

items.title: Written question from the North Galolhu member to the Minister of Tourism and Environment on the acquisition cost of islands and lagoons leased for tourism (July 2023 to July 2025)
items.outcome: written answer tabled; chair said it contained statistics and would be given to the member and published

items.title: Written question from the Maavashu member to the Minister of Foreign Affairs on a September 2025 memorandum of understanding between China and the Maldives
items.outcome: written answer tabled; talks on a further agreement ongoing, information to be shared when finished

items.title: First reading of a government bill to amend the Evidence Act (Law 2022/11), sponsored by the Bilehdhoo member Ahmed Aslam
Urgent matter submitted by the South Galolhu member under Rule 192
items.outcome: chair said it did not meet the conditions of Rule 192, so it would not be taken up as an urgent matter

items.title: Resolution from the Kendhoo member on delays in handing over the 4,000 Gedhoruveriya flats and the related land plots
items.outcome: debated; no decision in this part

items.title: Report of the Human Rights and Gender Committee on the President's nominee, Dr. Aishath Rameela, for the Human Rights Commission
items.outcome: report presented and debated, then put to a vote (see item 9.1)

items.title: Vote on appointing Dr. Aishath Rameela to the Human Rights Commission of the Maldives

speakers.name: Mohamed Ibrahim
positions: Asked the Housing minister when the Baarashu harbour works will begin and how long they will take.
Asked the Tourism minister the acquisition cost of islands and lagoons leased for tourism between July 2023 and July 2025.

speakers.name: Hussain Imran Latheef
positions: Said Malé and atoll members should not be set against each other, and that about 90 percent of the 4,000 flat recipients were long-time island-born Malé residents.
Said cases of flats obtained with false information are before the courts, and that the sponsor would not be taken seriously on Malé residents' rights.

speakers.name: Ahmed Shakir
positions: Asked the Foreign Minister for details of the September 2025 memorandum of understanding between China and the Maldives.

speakers.name: Ahmed Xamyr
positions: Said the government is already handling the flats and land issue well, and blamed earlier plots allocated from the sea for the current problems.
Said the President has promised that entitled people will get what they are due, whatever party they support.

speakers.name: Hassan Zareer
positions: Said the government is giving flats and plots to Malé residents without political favouritism.
Argued that about 9,200 plots given out without a clear system cost the state heavily compared with selling them at market rates.

speakers.name: Dr. Ahmed Shamheed
positions: Said the 4,000-flat problem dates from 2023 and stems from too few flats for demand, and that the housing plans need billions of dollars.
Questioned where the money will come from and called for a permanent, workable housing policy.

speakers.name: Hussain Hameed
positions: Said land and flats must be allocated under the rules, not outside them.
Argued that reclaiming one large area such as Rasmale is a better answer than many small reclamations.

speakers.name: Meekail Ahmed Nasym
positions: Said land already registered to Malé residents by the state must be respected by any government.
Called Rasmale a vanity project and said Parliament should hold judges accountable, disagreeing with the chair's ruling on his urgent matter.

speakers.name: Ibrahim Shujau
positions: Said the resolution does not fit current facts, because the earlier 4,000 flats were meant for those who were entitled.
Said the government will honour the President's promise to hand over land and flats to those entitled.

speakers.name: Ahmed Saleem
positions: Cited the caliph Umar's recovery of land granted outside the rules to argue that land rights must be handled fairly.
Said about 80 percent of the Hiya flats are rented out rather than lived in.

speakers.name: Mohamed Musthafa Ibrahim
positions: Said many Malé residents live in very cramped conditions and that land was shared unfairly under the previous government.
Said the present government is working to give Malé residents land and flats and expects a full housing solution within five years.

speakers.name: Mauroof Zakir
positions: Raised a point of order saying the remarks being made about him and Malé residents were false.

speakers.name: Hassan Mufeed Abdul Gadir
positions: Said members from the atolls do not oppose Malé residents getting land and flats, and rejected claims to the contrary.
Said the government is reclaiming the land and will hand it over to citizens, including those in the Greater Malé zone.

speakers.name: Ahmed Didi
positions: Said he supports the resolution, as the President promised a total housing solution but two years on no new flat foundations have been laid.
Said the promised number of units has been cut, and called on the government to prioritise building flats over other projects such as Rasmale.

speakers.name: Fathimath Sauda
positions: Presented the Human Rights and Gender Committee report recommending Dr. Aishath Rameela, who received over 90 percent of marks from committee members at interview.

speakers.name: Ibrahim Falah
positions: Supported the committee report, saying the nominee is well qualified.
As Majority Leader, said the government will hand over to Malé residents the land they already hold, as it stands.

speakers.name: Hussain Ziyad
positions: Supported the report but said the Human Rights Commission's budget is too small for its units to work, such as the whistleblower unit.
Asked Parliament to fund the commission properly and said spending on political matters should be redirected.

decisions: Dr. Aishath Rameela of G. Aabin was approved as a member of the Human Rights Commission of the Maldives by a vote of 63 to 0
The chair ruled the South Galolhu member's urgent matter did not meet the conditions of Rule 192 and would not be taken up
Milandhoo member Hassan Mufeed announced as replacing Manadhoo member Husnee Mubarik on the Judiciary Committee
Chair announced the next sitting for 30 October 2025 at 09:00, to present the 2026 state budget

votes.what: Appointment of Dr. Aishath Rameela as a member of the Human Rights Commission of the Maldives
